\begin{theorem}[Output accumulated from emitted symbols]
\lean{Complexity.output_runFrom_eq_flatMap}
\label{Complexity.output_runFrom_eq_flatMap}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.emitted, Complexity.snapshotAt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.outputSymbol, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_output}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite-state multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be
a binary input, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. The output after $t$ steps from the initial
configuration on $x$ is the concatenation, in order for times $s=0,\ldots,t-1$, of the
optional symbols emitted by the transition prescribed at the snapshot of the run at time
$s$; a halted snapshot contributes no symbol.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance by time]
\lean{Complexity.tableauAccepted}
\label{Complexity.tableauAccepted}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.emitted, Complexity.snapshotAt}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with a binary input alphabet, let $x$ be a finite
binary string, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. The acceptance indicator is true exactly when
there is some time $s<t$ at which the machine's snapshot on input $x$ emits the bit
true; otherwise it is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Ideal Tape Bits]
\lean{Complexity.idealTapeBits}
\label{Complexity.idealTapeBits}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.prevVisit, Complexity.snapEncode, Complexity.snapWidth, Complexity.snapshotAt}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean tapes, let $x$ be a finite Boolean
string, let $t\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\tau$ be a tape index of $M$. If there is no
previous visit of tape $\tau$ by time $t$, assign the list of $\mathrm{snapWidth}(M)+1$
false bits. Otherwise, assign a true bit followed by the encoding of the machine
snapshot at the previous visit.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Ideal source bits]
\lean{Complexity.idealSources}
\label{Complexity.idealSources}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.idealTapeBits, Complexity.inputBitAt, Complexity.inputPosAt, Complexity.snapEncode, Complexity.snapWidth, Complexity.snapshotAt, Complexity.tableauAccepted}
Let $M$ be a Turing machine with Boolean-valued symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean
string, and let $t$ be a natural number. Define the source list by concatenating: if
$t=0$, a list of $	ext{snapWidth}(M)$ false bits, and otherwise the encoding of the
configuration of $M$ on $x$ at time $t-1$; the three bits indicating respectively that
$t=0$, that the input head position at time $t$ on input $x$ contains an input bit, and
the value of that bit (taken to be false if there is no such bit); the ideal tape-bit
lists at time $t$ for each of the $M.k$ work tapes; and finally false if $t=0$, or the
indicator that $M$ has accepted $x$ by time $t-1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-length block extraction]
\lean{Complexity.CfgTableau.take_drop_flatMap_append}
\label{Complexity.CfgTableau.take_drop_flatMap_append}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $l$ be a finite list, let $g$ assign to each element of $l$ a list of length $c$,
and let $rest$ be any list. For every index $i$ with $i<|l|$, the block of length $c$
beginning at position $ic$ in the concatenation of the flattened lists $g(a)$, for $a$
in $l$, followed by $rest$, is exactly $g(l_i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Layout of a decoded tableau row]
\lean{Complexity.decode_layout}
\label{Complexity.decode_layout}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.snapWidth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let $w$ be the number
of possible snapshots of $M$. Suppose a Boolean list $\mathrm{pre}$ has length $w$, and
a Boolean list $F$ has length $k(w+1)$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$.
For any bits $a,b,c,d$, the list $\mathrm{pre} ++ [a,b,c] ++ F ++ [d]$ has prefix of
length $w$ equal to $\mathrm{pre}$; its entries at indices $w,w+1,w+2$ are respectively
$a,b,c$; dropping its first $w+3$ entries yields $F ++ [d]$; and its entry at index
$w+3+k(w+1)$ is $d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Recovering an optional Boolean value]
\lean{Complexity.option_isSome_getD}
\label{Complexity.option_isSome_getD}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every optional Boolean value $o$, replacing it by the optional value containing its
default-false value when it is present, and by no value when it is absent, returns $o$.
\end{theorem}

Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine whose head positions depend only on the input
length and time, let $x$ be a binary string, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Applying the
tableau update rule to the ideal source bits for $x$ at time $t$ yields the encoding of

\begin{theorem}[Tableau source values]
\lean{Complexity.tableauSources_map_getD}
\label{Complexity.tableauSources_map_getD}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.idealSources, Complexity.idealTapeBits, Complexity.inputBitAt, Complexity.inputPosAt, Complexity.prevVisit, Complexity.prevVisit_lt, Complexity.snapEncode, Complexity.snapWidth, Complexity.snapshotAt, Complexity.tableauAccepted, Complexity.tableauBlock, Complexity.tableauConst, Complexity.tableauSources, Complexity.tableauTapeSources, Complexity.tableauVertex}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a finite
Boolean string of length $n$, let $t\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $v$ be a finite list of
Boolean values. Assume that $v_i=x_i$ for every $i<|x|$, that the values at indices $n$
and $n+1$ are respectively false and true, and that for every $s<t$ the values read at
the tableau block for time $s$ form the machine-configuration encoding at time $s$,
while the value at the tableau vertex for time $s$ is the acceptance value at time $s$.
Then the values read from the tableau source indices at time $t$ equal the ideal source
list: they encode the preceding configuration (or consist of false values when $t=0$),
include the time-zero flag and the input symbol indicated by the input-head position,
give each work tape's information from its most recent visit to its current position (or
the prescribed blank information if there was no such visit), and include the previous
acceptance value (false when $t=0$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Values of the tableau gates]
\lean{Complexity.tableauGates_values}
\label{Complexity.tableauGates_values}
\leanok

\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input and output whose input-head
and work-tape-head positions at each time depend only on the input length. Let $x$ be a
finite Boolean string of length $n$, and let $t$ be a natural number. Evaluating the
tableau gates for $M,n,t$ with $x$ as the input gives $x_i$ at each input index $i$; the
next two vertices have values false and true, respectively. For every time $s<t$, the
values at the tableau block for time $s$ form the encoding of the machine configuration
at time $s$ on input $x$, and the tableau vertex for time $s$ records whether the
machine has emitted true at some time strictly before $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tableau circuit computes acceptance]

Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the binary alphabet whose input-head and

\begin{theorem}[Emission Characterizes a Computed Bit]
\lean{Complexity.decide_emits_eq_of_computesInTime}
\label{Complexity.decide_emits_eq_of_computesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.emitted, Complexity.output_runFrom_eq_flatMap, Complexity.snapshotAt, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine, let $x$ be a binary word, let $b$ be a bit,
and let $t$ be a natural number. If $M$ halts within $t$ steps on input $x$ with output
consisting of the single bit $b$, then the Boolean decision of whether some time $s<t$
has a snapshot whose selected transition emits $1$ is equal to $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Emission Detects the Language Indicator]
\lean{Complexity.decide_emits_eq_indicator}
\label{Complexity.decide_emits_eq_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.decide_emits_eq_of_computesInTime, Complexity.emitted, Complexity.snapshotAt, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine, $L$ a binary language,
$T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ a time bound, and suppose $M$ decides $L$ within time $T$.
For every binary word $x$, the Boolean decision of whether there is a time $s<T(|x|)$ at
which the transition selected from the run's snapshot emits the bit $1$ equals the
indicator of whether $x\in L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit simulation of an oblivious computation]
\lean{Complexity.exists_tableau_circuit}

Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine whose input-head position and work-tape head
positions after any fixed number of steps depend only on the input length. Suppose $M$
decides a language $L$ within time $T$. Then there is a constant $K\in\mathbb{N}$ such
that, for every $n$, there is a well-formed Boolean circuit with at most two inputs per
